templates.pattern: Light travels from air into a medium where its speed is [V] × 10⁶ m/s. What is the refractive index of the medium? (c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
Light hits a glass surface (refractive index [N]) from air. Using Snell's law, if sin of the angle of incidence is [SI] (as a decimal), what is the sin of the angle of refraction?
templates.explanation: Snell's law: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. With n₁=1 (air): sin θ₂ = sin θ₁ ÷ n₂ = 0.[SI] ÷ [N] = [RESULT]

templates.pattern: A glass block has refractive index [N]. What is the critical angle in degrees? (Use: sin C = 1 ÷ n, and these values: n=1.5 → 42°, n=2 → 30°, n=1.4 → 46°, n=1.8 → 34°)
templates.explanation: Critical angle C is found from sin C = 1 ÷ n. For n=[N], C = [RESULT]. Beyond this angle total internal reflection occurs.

templates.pattern: An object [H] cm tall is placed [U] cm from a converging lens of focal length [F] cm. Using the lens formula, what is the image distance v in cm?
templates.explanation: Lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f (with u negative). Rearranging: v = uF ÷ (u−F) = [U]×[F] ÷ ([U]−[F]) = [U*F] ÷ [U-F] = [RESULT] cm

templates.pattern: An image is formed [V] cm from a lens and the object is [U] cm from the lens. What is the magnification?
templates.explanation: Magnification = image distance ÷ object distance = [V] ÷ [U] = [RESULT]. A value greater than 1 means the image is larger than the object.

templates.pattern: A ray of light inside glass (refractive index [N]) hits the glass-air boundary at [A] degrees. The critical angle is [C] degrees. What happens to the ray?
templates.explanation: If the angle of incidence ([A]°) is greater than the critical angle ([C]°), total internal reflection occurs. If less, light refracts out into air.

templates.pattern: A converging lens of focal length [F] cm produces an image [V] cm from the lens. What is the object distance in cm?
templates.explanation: Lens formula rearranged: u = vF ÷ (v−F) = [V]×[F] ÷ ([V]−[F]) = [V*F] ÷ [V-F] = [RESULT] cm

templates.pattern: An object [H] cm tall produces an image [M] times magnified by a lens. What is the height of the image in cm?
templates.explanation: Image height = object height × magnification = [H] × [M] = [RESULT] cm

templates.pattern: Light travels through medium 1 (refractive index [N1]) into medium 2 (refractive index [N2]). If n1 > n2, what happens to the speed of light?
templates.explanation: Speed of light = c ÷ n. When moving from higher n ([N1]) to lower n ([N2]), n decreases so speed increases. Light bends away from the normal.

templates.pattern: A lens has a power of [P] dioptres. What is its focal length in cm?
templates.explanation: Power (dioptres) = 1 ÷ focal length (metres). Focal length = 1 ÷ [P] m = 100 ÷ [P] cm = [RESULT] cm
